2608.19125.title: Tuning the Stochastic Machine: A Systems Engineer's Operating Model for Human-AI Engineering
2608.19125.paper_summary: When an expert corrects an LLM assistant's error, the correction usually dies with the session, and the error class returns. I argue this is an operations problem, not a tooling problem: mechanisms for persisting corrections exist and are shipping, but the discipline for governing them -- versioning with provenance, recurrence monitoring, counter-metrics, retirement of stale rules -- does not. Writing as a systems engineer of thirty years, I map the LLM stack onto the machines my profession already operates (frozen silicon, firmware, loadable modules, persistent configuration, volatile memory), identify where the mapping fails (stochastic generation, configuration that binds only probabilistically, no general-purpose retirement (verification) stage by default), and derive from the failures a seven-principle operating discipline with an error loop at its core. Three cases from my own practice illustrate the mechanism, among them a control that silently became the exact harm it was built to prevent. I close with the measurement framework this view implies and the lab study required to test it.
2608.19125.paper_summary_zh: 當專家修正 LLM 助手的錯誤時，該修正通常隨著會話的結束而消失，錯誤類別又會回來。我認為這是一個操作問題，而不是工具問題：持久化修正的機制已經存在並且正在運行，但治理它們的紀律——版本控制與來源追溯、重複監控、反指標、過時規則的退休——卻不存在。作為一名擁有三十年經驗的系統工程師，我將 LLM 堆疊映射到我專業已經運作的機器上（冷凍矽、固件、可加載模塊、持久配置、易失性內存），識別映射失敗的地方（隨機生成、僅以概率綁定的配置、默認情況下沒有通用的退休（驗證）階段），並從這些失敗中推導出一個以錯誤循環為核心的七原則操作紀律。來自我自身實踐的三個案例說明了這一機制，其中一個控制默默地變成了它所建立的防止的確切危害。我以這一觀點所暗示的測量框架和測試所需的實驗室研究作結。
2608.19125.author: George Andrikopoulos et.al.
